grand_strategy.reading:
NATO is a strategy only in the sense that a coalition can have one: it does what
thirty-two governments can sign, and the signature is the product. Since 2022 its
Luttwakian logic has been straightforward at the top level (deter Russia, with
Article 5 as the whole point) and perverse in the levels that carry it. To keep the
one member that matters it has to make that member's complaint its own agenda -
more European money, more European forces, 'NATO 3.0' - and each concession
advertises how much of the deterrent was always American. The Ankara summit of
7-8 July 2026 settled the immediate question (Article 5 'ironclad', Russia the
long-term threat, EUR 70bn for Ukraine, over USD 50bn of procurements) in six
paragraphs, and left the structural ones open: Washington's posture review is due
to reach Hegseth on 6 November, Ukraine's door is neither shut nor opened, Spain
and Slovakia are outside the 5% logic, and the next summit, promised for Albania
by Rutte, has no date. Two signals that are not rows: the omission of China and of
any Ukraine-membership language from both declarations, and Rutte's repeated use of
the 'division of labour' with the EU as the way to make Europeans pay without calling
it a retreat. Read through Luttwak, the alliance's strength (the Article 5 promise
that everyone believes in enough to pay for) is also its weakness: the promise is
only as strong as the doubts of the one guarantor, so the alliance spends its
political capital managing the guarantor rather than the adversary.

stances.note: Rival, not adversary, in the ontology's terms. The 2022 Strategic Concept names Russia 'the most significant and direct threat' and the Ankara declaration (8 Jul 2026) 'the long-term threat', Eastern Sentry (12 Sep 2025), Baltic Sentry (Jan 2025) and two Article 4 sessions in September 2025 (Poland, Estonia) show the contest; NATO suspended practical cooperation in April 2014 and expelled eight Russian officials in October 2021, after which Moscow closed its mission. But NATO's declared aim is deterrence and defence, not the end of the Russian state or regime, and the channel for dialogue is kept formally open; Peskov himself said Moscow stays open to dialogue when there is a chance for constructive engagement. A threat label in an official text is the source for the hostile reading, the grade follows the structure (a standing deterrence contest, no allied war aim against Russia). Trend cooling: airspace violations (Estonia MiG-31s, 19 Sep 2025) and Russian drones in Poland rose in 2025-26. Bond - grievance: Moscow's reading of enlargement as encirclement, and NATO's of 2014 and 2022 as betrayal.
